Dehumidifiers function to eliminate excess moisture from the air, making your home more comfortable at all times. On one side of a common dehumidifier is a fan that sucks in humid air from vents on the opposing side. As the humid air enters the appliance it is met by a refrigerated evaporator. This part of the machine condenses the moisture in the air on to the surface of the evaporator, where it later drains into a reservoir. Here’s some more information on how dehumidifiers work!

The air, still being sucked through by the fan, then passes through a hot condenser, and is then returned to the room to disperse the still existing moisture. The process is repeated until the desired level of humidity is achieved. This can ensure that you and your family are comfortable at all times.
What Issues Do These Units Solve?
Dehumidifiers effectively control four main problems associated with high air humidity:

items: Less bacteria: Moisture is an ideal conductor for foul odors, allergens, pathogens and other airborne nose and throat irritants. Many common illnesses spread in this manner. Dehumidifiers prevent the spread of these bacteria from the start.
Mold prevention: Mold and mildew thrive almost exclusively due to moisture. This growth can be a serious health concern, which can result in costly repairs for your home.
Bug elimination: Various bugs, including destructive ones like termites, prefer to breed in damp environments. If left unaddressed, these creepy crawlers will destroy your house from the inside out.
Better food preservation: Food also tends to decompose at a faster rate in a humid room. High moisture levels can easily spell out a loss in time, money, and energy.
